_meta.indication: KISQALI is indicated in combination with an aromatase inhibitor as initial endocrine-based therapy for the treatment of postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced or metastatic breast cancer

pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: International, multi-center, randomized (1:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled trial of ribociclib plus letrozole versus placebo plus letrozole
pivotal_trials.population: Postmenopausal women with HR-positive, HER2-negative advanced breast cancer who received no prior therapy for advanced disease
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary endpoint was progression-free survival (PFS) as assessed by the local investigator per RECIST v1.1
pivotal_trials.n: 668 patients randomized (334 ribociclib plus letrozole; 334 placebo plus letrozole)
pivotal_trials.result: At the interim analysis, median PFS was not evaluable (95% CI 19.3, NE) for ribociclib plus letrozole vs 14.7 months (95% CI 13.0, 16.5) for placebo plus letrozole; HR 0.556 (95% CI: 0.429, 0.720); p < 0.0001

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (incidence ≥20%) are neutropenia, nausea, fatigue, diarrhea, leukopenia, alopecia, vomiting, constipation, headache and back pain. Neutropenia occurred in 75% (Grade 3 50%, Grade 4 10%) and nausea in 52% of KISQALI plus letrozole patients. Key labeled warnings are QT prolongation, hepatobiliary toxicity, and neutropenia.
target_moa: Ribociclib is an orally bioavailable small-molecule inhibitor of cyclin-dependent kinases 4 and 6 (CDK4/6); it induces G1 phase cell-cycle arrest in pRb-positive breast cancer cells by inhibiting Rb phosphorylation

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was required

summary.text: KISQALI (ribociclib) received breakthrough therapy designation (August 2, 2016) and was reviewed as a Priority NDA, receiving regular (full) approval on March 13, 2017 based on a statistically significant PFS improvement in the Phase 3 MONALEESA-2 trial; no advisory committee was required and no REMS was required.

citations.quote: **August 2, 2016:** FDA granted the breakthrough therapy designation based on the fact that breast cancer meets the criteria for a serious or life-threatening disease and the preliminary clinical evidence generated by Study A2301 appeared to demonstrated substantial improvement in PFS compared with existing therapies.

In conclusion, ribociclib in combination with letrozole demonstrated a statistically significant improvement in PFS in a large, randomized, double blind study. requirement.text: 3168-1: Conduct a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of an alternative dosing regimen for ribociclib after evaluation of ECG, PK and efficacy data from ongoing MONALEESA-3 (CLEE011F2301) and MONALEESA-7 (CLEE011E2301) to mitigate QT prolongation risk

citations.quote: 3168-1 Conduct a clinical trial to assess the efficacy and safety of an alternative dosing regimen for ribociclib after evaluation of ECG, PK and efficacy data from ongoing MONALEESA-3 (CLEE011F2301) and MONALEESA-7 (CLEE011E2301) studies. The objective of studying an alternative dosing regimen is to mitigate the risks for QT prolongation without compromising efficacy. The primary safety assessments should include QT prolongation, hepatobiliary toxicities, and neutropenia. The primary efficacy endpoint should be objective response rate (ORR).
